title: DG cone rotation by an A-linear homotopy equivalence
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $K_A$ for the category of these modules with degree-preserving $A$-linear chain maps modulo homotopies $f-g=dh+hd$, where $h$ is $A$-linear of degree $-1$. Shifts have $M[k]^i=M^{i+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_M$, and the unchanged right action. For a chain map $f:X\to Y$, put $C(f)^i=Y^i\oplus X^{i+1}$, $d_{C(f)}(y,x)=(d_Yy+f(x),-d_Xx)$, with componentwise right action. Put $i_f(y)=(y,0)$ and $p_f(y,x)=x$. Write $T_f$ for the triangle $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow{i_f}C(f)\xrightarrow{-p_f}X[1]$ in $K_A$. For every $f:X\to Y$, the rotation $(Y,C(f),X[1],i_f,-p_f,-f[1])$ of $T_f$ is isomorphic to $T_{i_f}$ in the category of triangles of $K_A$, with identity components on $Y$ and $C(f)$. More explicitly, in coordinates $C(i_f)^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}\oplus Y^{n+1}$ the maps $q(y,x,y')=-x$ and $s(x)=(0,-x,f(x))$ are $A$-linear chain maps $C(i_f)\rightleftarrows X[1]$ inverse up to $A$-linear homotopy, with $q s=1$, $q i_{i_f}=-p_f$, and $(-p_{i_f})s=-f[1]$. The inverse rotation $(C(f)[-1],X,Y,p_f[-1],f,i_f)$ is likewise isomorphic to the standard cone triangle $T_{p_f[-1]}$, with identity components on its first two objects.

source.place: Tag 09KB, lemma-rotate-cone; Tag 09KC, lemma-rotate-triangle; Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, proof of TR2. The explicit maps are the cone-coordinate formulation of these rotations, with the -p convention of Tag 09KF, lemma-the-same-up-to-isomorphisms.

proof.text: All constructions below use the unchanged right action in the statement. It makes a shift a DG module: for $m\in M[k]^n$, $(-1)^kd_M(ma)=(-1)^kd_M(m)a+(-1)^{k+n+k}m\,d_A(a)=d_{M[k]}(m)a+(-1)^nm\,d_A(a)$. The same calculation in the two cone coordinates gives its Leibniz rule, and $d_{C(f)}^2(y,x)=(d_Yf(x)-f(d_Xx),0)=0$. Thus all the following iterated cones and shifts are DG modules. Every coordinate formula below is additive and $A$-linear because it uses only projections, inclusions, signs and the $A$-linear map $f$; the homotopies have degree $-1$. No differential is assumed to be $A$-linear.

source.place: definition-shift and definition-cone, checked directly for right modules; Tag 09KF, lemma-the-same-up-to-isomorphisms (signed cone convention).

proof.text: Put $E=C(i_f)$. For $(y,x,y')\in E^n=Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}\oplus Y^{n+1}$ its differential is $D(y,x,y')=(d_Yy+fx+y',-d_Xx,-d_Yy')$. Consequently $qD(y,x,y')=d_Xx=d_{X[1]}q(y,x,y')$. Also $Ds(x)=(0,d_Xx,-f(d_Xx))=s(-d_Xx)=s(d_{X[1]}x)$. This proves that the specified $q$ and $s$ are chain maps. They satisfy $qs=1$ and $sq(y,x,y')=(0,x,-fx)$.

Define $H:E^n\to E^{n-1}$ by $H(y,x,y')=(0,0,y)$. Then $DH(y,x,y')=(y,0,-d_Yy)$ and $HD(y,x,y')=(0,0,d_Yy+fx+y')$. Hence $DH+HD=(y,0,fx+y')=1_E-sq$. The maps $[q]$ and $[s]$ in $K_A$ are therefore inverse. Moreover $qi_{i_f}(y,x)=-x=-p_f(y,x)$ and $(-p_{i_f})s(x)=-fx=-f[1](x)$, proving all the explicit identities requested.

source.place: Tag 09KF, lemma-the-same-up-to-isomorphisms (1), contraction; Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, forward TR2.

proof.text: For the remaining triangle square, let $J:E^n\to Y[1]^{n-1}=Y^n$ be $J(y,x,y')=-y$. The homotopy equation is $d_{Y[1]}J+JD=-fx-y'=(-p_{i_f})-(-f[1])q$. Thus $(1_Y,1_{C(f)},[q])$ is a morphism from $T_{i_f}$ to the rotation of $T_f$: its first square is the identity, its second is $qi_{i_f}=-p_f$, and its third is the displayed homotopy. Its inverse has components $(1_Y,1_{C(f)},[s])$: cancel $[q]$ in the same three square equations using $[q][s]=1=[s][q]$. This is the claimed triangle isomorphism with the first two components fixed.

source.place: Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, forward TR2; Tags 09KB and 09KF, with the minus projection convention.

proof.text: For inverse rotation put $U=C(f)[-1]$ and $g=p_f[-1]:U\to X$, so $g(y,x)=x$. Write $F=C(g)^n=X^n\oplus Y^n\oplus X^{n+1}$, with differential $D'(u,y,x)=(d_Xu+x,d_Yy+fx,-d_Xx)$. Define $r:F\to Y$ by $r(u,y,x)=fu-y$ and $t:Y\to F$ by $t(y)=(0,-y,0)$. Then $rD'=f(d_Xu)-d_Yy=d_Yr$ and $D't(y)=(0,-d_Yy,0)=t(d_Yy)$; also $rt=1$ and $tr(u,y,x)=(0,y-fu,0)$. For $H'(u,y,x)=(0,0,u)$, $D'H'=(u,fu,-d_Xu)$ and $H'D'=(0,0,d_Xu+x)$, giving $D'H'+H'D'=1_F-tr$. Hence $[r]$ and $[t]$ are inverse in $K_A$.

source.place: Tag 09KC, lemma-rotate-triangle, expanded in cone coordinates; Tag 09KH, lemma-homotopy-category-pre-triangulated, inverse TR2; Tag 09KF, signed convention.

proof.text: The inverse rotation is $(U,X,Y,g,f,i_f)$, since its first arrow is $-(-p_f)[-1]=g$. We have $ri_g=f$ and $(-p_g)t=i_f$ strictly. Identify $U[1]=C(f)$. For $J':F^n\to C(f)^{n-1}$ given by $J'(u,y,x)=(0,-u)$, one has $d_{C(f)}J'=(-fu,d_Xu)$ and $J'D'=(0,-d_Xu-x)$. Thus $dJ'+J'D'=(-fu,-x)=(-p_g)-i_fr$. Consequently $(1_U,1_X,[r])$ is a morphism from $T_g$ to the inverse rotation, with the first square tautological and the other two established above. Its componentwise inverse $(1_U,1_X,[t])$ satisfies the reverse square equations by cancellation. This proves the inverse-rotation isomorphism, with identity components on its first two objects.

A DG module over a general DG algebra is not such a complex of A-modules: its differential obeys the Leibniz rule rather than A-linearity. Forgetting to abelian groups loses A-linear maps and homotopies. A DG-action lift of the cone identities is a real argument, not a one-line specialization.
